Byomkesh.description: The protagonist, a renowned detective known for his sharp intellect and sense of justice; often referred to as a 'truth-seeker.'

Ajit.description: The narrator and close companion of Byomkesh, who documents their adventures and assists in investigations.

Rameswarbabu.description: A wealthy, humorous elderly man whose mysterious will is central to the story; 'babu' is a respectful suffix used for men.

Kumudini.description: Rameswarbabu’s second wife, described as obese and childless, with eccentric habits.

Kusheswar.description: Rameswarbabu’s son from his first marriage, depicted as effete and henpecked.

Nalini.description: Rameswarbabu’s daughter from his first marriage, estranged from the family after marrying against their wishes.

Labanya.description: Kusheswar’s wife, who dominates the household and is antagonistic towards Nalini.

Dr Ashim Sen.description: The family physician and friend, who has attended to Rameswarbabu for decades and acts as a witness to the will.

Devnath.description: Nalini’s husband, a middle-class man with a modest income.

Inspector Halder.description: The local police inspector who assists Byomkesh in searching for the will.

Putiram.description: The domestic help in Byomkesh’s household, responsible for cleaning and errands.

Bengali New Year.description: A major festival marking the start of the Bengali calendar year, celebrated with greetings and gifts.

Dussehra.description: A Hindu festival celebrating the victory of good over evil, observed across India.

Lakshmi.description: The Hindu goddess of wealth and prosperity, often referenced in connection with fortune.

Mahabharata.description: One of the two great Indian epics, chronicling the Kurukshetra war and the fate of the Kaurava and Pandava princes.

Ramayana.description: An ancient Indian epic narrating the life of Prince Rama, his exile, and the rescue of his wife Sita.

Grandfather Bheeshma.description: A revered elder and warrior from the Mahabharata, known for his wisdom and vow of celibacy.

Dasaratha.description: The king of Ayodhya and father of Rama in the Ramayana, known for his tragic old age.

Calcutta.description: Calcutta, now officially known as Kolkata, is a major city in eastern India and the primary setting for the story.

Vivekananda Road.description: A prominent road in Kolkata, named after the spiritual leader Swami Vivekananda.

Bagbazaar.description: A historic neighborhood in north Kolkata, referenced as the location of Rameswarbabu’s residence.

Shyamdhan Mitra Lane.description: A street in Kolkata, given as Rameswarbabu's address.

Harrison Road.description: A major thoroughfare in Kolkata (now Mahatma Gandhi Road), mentioned as the location of one of Rameswarbabu’s houses.

Shyampukur.description: A locality in north Kolkata, referenced as the site of Rameswarbabu’s residence.

Durga Puja.description: The most significant festival in Bengal, celebrating the goddess Durga.

betel leaf.description: A leaf from the betel plant, commonly chewed in India with areca nut and other ingredients as a mild stimulant.

Baisakh.description: The first month of the Bengali calendar, during which the Bengali New Year is celebrated.

monogrammed.description: Bearing a design composed of one or more letters, typically the initials of a name, used as an identifying mark.

intestate.description: A term for dying without having made a legal will.
